question.text: Mauryan Capital has computed PV of explicit-period FCFs = INR 450 crore and PV of Terminal Value = INR 850 crore for investee Himalaya Tech. Outstanding debt on valuation date = INR 120 crore; Cash = INR 30 crore. What is the Equity Value?

explanation.text: The Logic: Enterprise Value (the debt-free, cash-free value of the operating business) = PV of explicit-period FCFs + PV of Terminal Value = 450 + 850 = INR 1,300 crore. Equity Value = EV - Net Debt = 1,300 - (120 - 30) = 1,300 - 90 = INR 1,210 crore. Net debt (debt minus cash) is deducted from EV to derive equity value. The Trap: INR 1,300 crore is pure EV and forgets the debt deduction. INR 1,180 crore subtracts gross debt without adding cash back. INR 1,150 crore double-adjusts the bridge items. Note: 'Net of cash' deliberately credits surplus cash back to equity holders — gross debt overstates the senior claim against EV.
